profile_ab_ctx128.method: same model, same context, same seed, same prompt; profile is the only variable; 3 trials each
findings: the CLI banner is correct and the --profile help text is wrong: the default is NOT bit-identical, it runs the q4k-predec lm_head while exact runs f16
fast buys 0.6% over default, so the f16-scales lever is worth nothing here
exact issues 96 FEWER dispatches (339 vs 435) and is 6.8% SLOWER, which is direct same-model evidence that dispatch count is not the wall

byte_scaling_ctx512.MODEL_BREAKS: 841 GB/s exceeds the assumed 736 GB/s roof, which is impossible
byte_scaling_ctx512.reading: either the 736 constant is wrong (it is hard-coded at lab/operators/gravity_flop_ledger.py:24 with no sealed receipt) or the two-point linear fit is invalid because attention cost differs between the points. The ctx128 fit is physically plausible; this one is not, and is reported rather than dropped.

headline: the weight-bandwidth path is already near optimal at roughly 89% of the assumed roof; 63% of the token at ctx128 and 77% at ctx512 is fixed per-token cost that quantization cannot touch

consequences_for_the_kernel_plan.K2_quantized_matvec_sweep: LOW value here: bandwidth efficiency is already high, and Q6 vs Q4 shows bytes barely move the clock
consequences_for_the_kernel_plan.K4_K5_K7_fusion_residency_tokengraph: HIGH value: they attack the 23.3 ms fixed cost, which is the actual wall
consequences_for_the_kernel_plan.K8_representation: cannot reach TG20 for this model, because fixed cost alone is 23.3 ms and TG20 is 20 ms
consequences_for_the_kernel_plan.TG20_verdict: unreachable by quantization alone; requires removing fixed per-token cost first

contention.note: all comparisons are same-model paired A/B under identical contention, which is the admissible form
